test: Join crm_quotes (closed: won/lost/expired) to erp_customers.discount_pct and to quote-level markdown (any crm_quote_lines.markdown_pct > 0, and avg markdown). (1) Win rate by customer discount_pct band; (2) rep win rates raw vs within discount band, branch and quote-size band (spread of rep rates, and a rep effect after standardising each rep's expected win rate from discount x branch x size cells); (3) markdown vs no-markdown win rate within the same customer (customer fixed-effect style: compare per-customer differences), and by markdown depth; (4) check over time; (5) size lost-on-price value per year and the markdown dollars given on won quotes.
support: Win rate rises (or varies) clearly with discount_pct; rep spread shrinks substantially (e.g. range halves) once expected rate from customer discount/branch/size is removed; within-customer markdown vs no-markdown difference near zero.
weaken: Rep spread mostly survives controls; win rate flat across discount_pct; markdown quotes win clearly more often within customer.
expect: Moderate confidence that markdowns show no lift (q119 already shows ~0.43 both ways). Less sure discount_pct explains rep spread: rep 72's low discount is one data point; I expect discount to explain some but not all of the spread, and rep spread may partly be noise given ~15k quotes per rep (binomial SE ~0.004, so 0.36-0.53 is not noise). Overall I lean that the hypothesis is partly true: markdowns don't buy wins, but rep differences persist after discount controls.
